February, 2024

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:13628
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15150 of 2023
Applicant :- Shamim
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Raman Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None turned up on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.

2. In terms of the FIR, a missing person report was lodged alleging that the grand-daughter of the informant was missing, subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim disclosed her age as 17 years and stated that she had gone along with the applicant to Mumbai and thereafter she stayed with him and physical relations were also formed in between them.
In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she admitted that she was carrying love affair with the applicant.

entities.text: Shamim vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the age of the victim is 13 years, however there is no definite document to conclusively determine the age of the victim as prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed there-under.

4. Considering the two statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 23.08.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Shamim be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 223 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) IPC, Section 3/4(2) POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, Police Station Jarwal Road, District Bahraich, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024 Arun  Shamim vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152775557/
